correctness.rationale: On the repaired domains, the sign average is the product of the odd-multiplicity indicators and counts labeled rim words in bijection with indexed closed walks. Sign complementation pairs terms only as used when n≡k mod 2, yielding integer counts B₄ and B₅ there. The local neighborhood condition gives cyclic distance-two properness and the hub gives odd rim classes. Small rims force singleton classes, three colors force period three (and odd class sizes precisely for n≡3 mod 6), and the parity, size bounds and verified +6 witness extension fix all remaining optimal palette sizes. The 14-rim has six rim colors and the independently reproduced rim count 9,344,160 gives 65,409,120 after seven hub choices. In the signed asymptotics all states communicate (including reversal of any pair with a four-color walk); 3- and 4-cycles ensure primitivity. The equality condition for spectral-radius comparison forces one common phase on the products along 3-cycles. Comparing triples with two common colors forces all signs equal. Only the all-positive and all-negative terms therefore contribute the leading terms, with factor 2^(1−k) on the repaired parity domains before the hub factor.
residual_risks: The exact arithmetic replay checks the matrix factorizations and finite exceptional count; the argument with the parity projection and spectral comparison proves the unbounded claims.

Manattu–Vinay–Lakshmanan wheel palette theorem in arXiv:2602.03259
value.rationale: The wheel is a canonical family with a known optimum, but an optimum palette is not a measure of how many optimal configurations exist. The exact formula exposes a qualitative difference: two odd residue classes have exponential growth while the third has a fixed 24 configurations. It also counts the exact exceptional order using the graph's actual optimum rather than extrapolating a generic branch. The parity-domain correction leaves that worthwhile comparison intact.
residual_risks: The interpreted counts are for distinguished vertices and named colors only; no symmetry-orbit census is claimed.
